hood_landmark.Niederdorf: Cabaret Voltaire, birthplace of the Dada movement
hood_landmark.Langstrasse (Kreis 4): Langstrasse itself — the gritty, multicultural bar and nightlife strip

avoid.reason: Keep usual awareness around Langstrasse's nightlife and red-light strip late at night, and watch for pickpockets at the main station (HB).

hood_desc: Altstadt is Zurich's historic medieval old town core with cobbled lanes, churches and upscale shops, ideal for first-time visitors and history lovers who want to be in the heart of the action.
Niederdorf is the lively pedestrian old-town quarter on the east bank of the Limmat, packed with bars, restaurants and nightlife that suits younger travelers and social crowds.

Langstrasse in Kreis 4 is the gritty, multicultural former red-light district now reborn as Zurich's edgiest nightlife and bar hub, best for night owls and those wanting an alternative, unpolished scene.
Zurich-West in Kreis 5 is a former industrial zone turned trendy district of galleries, design shops, clubs and the Freitag tower, perfect for creatives and a hip, urban crowd.
Seefeld is an affluent, relaxed lakeside neighborhood on the east shore with chic cafes, boutiques and easy lake access, well suited to families and travelers seeking a quieter, upscale base.

water.note: Tap water is safe and often sourced straight from Alpine springs, even from public fountains.

transit.pay: Buy tickets before boarding from machines at every stop or in the ZVV or SBB Mobile apps (EasyRide check-in). A single city-zone ticket is about CHF 4.60 (~US$5.70) and a 24-hour pass about CHF 9.20; the tourist Zurich Card includes all transit. One ticket covers trams, buses, S-Bahn and boats - there are no tap gates, but inspections are frequent.
transit.hours: Trams and trains run about 5am-12:30am daily; on Friday and Saturday nights an all-night network of trams, buses and S-Bahn runs at no extra charge.

food.name: Zuercher Geschnetzeltes
food.desc: Strips of veal and mushrooms in a white wine and cream sauce, served with crisp roesti. The city's own dish.

places.name: Zeughauskeller
places.note: Beer hall in a 15th-century armoury; big portions, fast service, long shared tables.

places.name: Kronenhalle
places.note: Wood-panelled dining room hung with Chagall and Picasso; the grand version.

places.name: Swiss Chuchi
places.note: Reliable all-rounder for Swiss classics in the old town; book ahead.

food.name: Cheese fondue
food.desc: Gruyere and Vacherin melted with white wine and kirsch, eaten with bread cubes. A winter dish, and locals mean it.

places.name: Le Dezaley
places.note: Vaudois restaurant in two medieval houses; the fondue address most locals name first.

places.name: Chaesalp
places.note: Hillside chalet above the city, rustic and hugely popular for fondue and raclette.

places.name: Swiss Chuchi
places.note: Central, open late and does a good moitie-moitie for first-timers.

food.name: Roesti
food.desc: Grated potato pressed into a pan and fried golden. Served plain with meat, or topped with cheese, bacon and a fried egg.

places.name: Zunfthaus zur Waag
places.note: Guild house on Muensterhof since 1636; refined Swiss cooking in a historic hall.

places.name: Zeughauskeller
places.note: Roesti with sausages or geschnetzeltes; cheap by Zurich standards.

places.name: Restaurant Schipfe 16
places.note: Simple riverside spot in the oldest quarter, with terrace tables over the Limmat.

food.name: Zuercher Bratwurst
food.desc: Fat veal sausage grilled over wood and served with a crusty buerli roll and mustard. Eaten standing up, no plate needed.

places.name: Sternen Grill
places.note: Zurich institution since 1963; famously fierce house mustard, queue moves fast.

places.name: Vorderer Sternen
places.note: The other half of the same corner, grilling over wood; locals argue over which is better.

food.name: Luxemburgerli
food.desc: Sprungli's featherlight mini macarons, smaller and softer than the Paris kind, in a rotating palette of flavours.

places.name: Confiserie Sprungli
places.note: The 1836 flagship where Luxemburgerli were invented; buy by the box or eat upstairs.

places.name: Sprungli Hauptbahnhof
places.note: Station branch, useful for a last box before the train; same product.

food.name: Birchermuesli
food.desc: Invented by a Zurich doctor around 1900: oats soaked in milk or cream with grated apple, lemon, nuts and berries.

places.name: Hiltl
places.note: The world's oldest vegetarian restaurant, open since 1898; breakfast buffet included.

places.name: Cafe Sprungli
places.note: Serves it in a proper coffee-house setting overlooking Bahnhofstrasse.

places.name: Babu's Bakery
places.note: Modern all-day bakery cafe near the station with good muesli and cakes.

food.name: Zurich wine
food.desc: Vineyards ring the lake; Raeuschling is the local white, crisp and lightly floral, with Pinot Noir the main red.

places.name: Zunfthaus zur Waag
places.note: Strong list of Zurich-canton wines to drink with traditional Swiss dishes.

places.name: Kronenhalle Bar
places.note: Art-lined bar beside the restaurant; a Zurich rite of passage for an evening drink.

places.name: Weinbar Rosso
places.note: Under-the-railway wine bar in the industrial district, relaxed and well priced.

food.name: Swiss beer
food.desc: Zurich's own Turbinenbraeu and Hurlimann plus a growing craft scene, best drunk outdoors in the old industrial west.

places.name: Bierhalle Wolf
places.note: Old-school beer hall off Bahnhofstrasse with brass band nights and litre steins.

places.name: Frau Gerolds Garten
places.note: Container-and-garden bar under the viaduct; the summer drinking spot in the city.

places.name: Turbinenbraeu
places.note: Independent city brewery; tap sales and tours for a genuinely local pint.

landmarks: Grossmünster
This twin-towered Romanesque church dominates Zürich's skyline and marks the birthplace of the Swiss Reformation. Climb its tower for postcard-perfect views over the Limmat River and old town.
Fraumünster Church
Famous for its stunning stained-glass windows designed by Marc Chagall, this abbey church is a hidden gem of artistic splendor. The jewel-toned light pouring through the glass is unforgettable.
Lake Zürich (Zürichsee)
This sparkling alpine lake framed by distant mountains is the city's playground, ideal for lakeside walks, swimming, or a scenic boat cruise. Sunset views here are simply spectacular.
Bahnhofstrasse
One of the world's most exclusive shopping avenues, this elegant boulevard runs from the main train station to the lake. Its manicured trees and grand facades make for a quintessential Zürich stroll.
St. Peter's Church
Home to the largest clock face in Europe, this landmark church tower is a defining feature of the old town skyline. Its oversized clock hands have been keeping time since the 18th century.
Lindenhof
Perched on a hill above the old town, this shaded plaza was once a Roman fort and offers one of the best free panoramic views in the city. Locals gather here to play chess and watch the sunset.
Uetliberg Mountain
Zürich's very own 'house mountain' is a short train ride away and rewards hikers with sweeping views of the Alps and the lake below. It's the perfect escape for photographers chasing golden hour.
Old Town (Altstadt)
A maze of cobblestone lanes, guild houses, and hidden courtyards straddles both banks of the Limmat River. Wandering here feels like stepping into a medieval storybook.
Kunsthaus Zürich

One of Switzerland's premier art museums houses masterpieces from Monet to Munch inside striking architecture, including a bold Chipperfield-designed extension. Art lovers could spend an entire day here.
Swiss National Museum
Housed in a fairy-tale castle-like building near the main station, this museum traces Switzerland's cultural history through rich collections. Its turrets alone make for a great photo.

train.note: All these trains leave from Zürich HB. Day Railjets to Vienna also run. In summer 2026 some Nightjet/EuroNight services toward Vienna, Budapest and Zagreb are diverted or retimed by engineering works (mid-June to mid-October) - check times when booking.

bus.note: International coaches use the Sihlquai coach station just behind Zürich HB. FlixBus is by far the main operator; carry your passport/ID as Switzerland is in Schengen but not the EU customs union.

ferry.note: Switzerland is landlocked - no international ferries from Zurich. Lake Zurich boats run by ZSG (https://www.zsg.ch/en) are scenic local excursions only.

half.name: Lucerne
half.blurb: Postcard lakeside city with a covered wooden bridge, old town and mountain backdrop.

half.name: Rhine Falls
half.blurb: Europe's most powerful waterfall thundering over rocks, with boat rides to the central crag.

half.name: Interlaken
half.blurb: Alpine resort town set between two lakes, gateway to the Jungfrau peaks.

half.name: Bern
half.blurb: Switzerland's medieval capital with arcaded streets, a clock tower and riverside old town.

half.name: Mount Titlis
half.blurb: Glacier-capped summit reached by rotating cable car, with snow, caves and cliff walk.

half.name: Basel
half.blurb: Rhine-side city famed for its art museums, colorful old town and cathedral.
